measures.questionText: Shall the North Smithfield Home Rule Charter be amended to modify Article II, Section 2 and Article IV, Section 1 to provide that, commencing December 1, 2028: • The Town Council shall consist of five (5) members elected at-large at regular biennial elections in even-numbered years. Except as provided below for the 2028 regular election, each member shall serve a four-year term and until a successor is elected and qualified, and at each regular election only those seats whose terms are expiring shall be filled; • At the 2028 regular election only, the three (3) candidates receiving the highest number of votes shall be elected to four-year terms expiring December 1, 2032, and the two (2) candidates receiving the next highest number of votes shall be elected to two-year terms expiring December 1, 2030, so that Town Council terms are staggered thereafter; • The existing Charter provision limiting elected officials to eight (8) consecutive years in the same elected office shall remain in effect; • A person who has served eight (8) consecutive years in the same elected office shall remain ineligible to seek election to that office until at least four (4) years have elapsed following the expiration of such service; and • As a one-time transition to staggered Town Council terms, any Town Council member elected in 2028 shall be permitted to serve the full term to which elected notwithstanding the eight-consecutive-year limitation, and any Town Council member elected to a two-year term in 2028 shall be eligible to seek election to a four-year Town Council term at the 2030 regular election, with such two-year term not counted toward the Charter’s eight-consecutive-year limitation?
measures.officialStatement: This amendment would modify Articles II and IV of the Home Rule Charter. The amendment would establish staggered four-year terms for members of the Town Council beginning December 1, 2028. At the 2028 regular election, the three candidates receiving the highest number of votes would serve four-year terms ending in 2032 and the two candidates receiving the next highest number of votes would serve two-year terms ending in 2030. Thereafter, all Town Council seats would be filled for staggered four-year terms, with three seats elected in 2032 and every four years after that, and two seats elected in 2030 and every four years after that. The amendment would retain the existing Charter provision limiting elected officials to eight consecutive years in the same elected office and would continue to require a four-year break in service before a person who has reached that limit may again seek election to the same office. The amendment would also establish a one-time transition provision to implement staggered Town Council terms. Under this provision, any Town Council member elected in 2028 would be permitted to complete the term to which elected even if such service would otherwise exceed the Charter’s eight-consecutive-year limitation. In addition, a Town Council member elected to a two-year transitional term in 2028 would be eligible to seek election to a four-year term in 2030, and the transitional two-year term would not be counted toward the Charter’s eight-consecutive-year limitation.

measures.questionText: Shall the Home Rule Charter of the Town of North Smithfield be amended by revising Article XIII, Section 1 (Personnel Board) to remove the existing prohibition that members “shall not hold or be a candidate for any other public office or position” and related political activity restrictions, and to instead provide that Personnel Board members shall not hold or be candidates for elective office within the Town of North Smithfield, with resignation required upon candidacy, while permitting such members to hold or seek elective office in other municipalities or at the state or federal level as allowed by Rhode Island law and also be amended to reflect the accuracy of the current duties of the Personnel Board which have been modified since the last update?
measures.officialStatement: This amendment would update Article XIII, Section 1 of the Charter governing the Personnel Board by: • Removing the current blanket prohibition on holding or being a candidate for any public office and certain political activities; • Replacing it with a narrower restriction prohibiting Personnel Board members from holding or running for elective office within the Town of North Smithfield; • Requiring resignation from the Board if a member becomes a candidate for Town elective office; • Allowing members to hold or seek elective office in other municipalities or at the state or federal level, consistent with Rhode Island law; • The duties of the Personnel Board have been updated to reflect the actual responsibilities of the Personnel Board, removing responsibilities that are now performed by different entities; and • The amendment is intended to prevent conflicts of interest within Town government while aligning the Charter with constitutional requirements articulated in cases such as Broadrick v. Oklahoma, Magill v. Lynch, and Cranston Teachers Alliance Local No. 1704 AFT v. Miele.

measures.questionText: Shall the North Smithfield Home Rule Charter be amended to replace Section 12 of Article XV with a new Section, establishing a Department of Facilities and Capital Assets, headed by a Director of Facilities appointed by the Town Administrator, responsible for: • Managing, maintaining, repairing, and planning all municipal buildings, grounds, and infrastructure; • Developing a Capital Improvement Plan; • Overseeing construction and renovation projects; • Managing utilities and energy programs; • Ensuring compliance with environmental standards; • Preparing and administering the Department’s operating budget; and to renumber the current Section 12 as Section 13?
measures.officialStatement: This amendment would replace Section 12 of Article XV to establish a Department of Facilities and Capital Assets, headed by a Director of Facilities. The Department would provide professional oversight for: • Maintenance, repair, and long-term planning of municipal buildings, grounds, and infrastructure; • Capital projects, including construction and renovation; • Utilities management, energy programs, and environmental compliance; • Preparation and administration of the Department’s operating budget. • The amendment also renumbers the current Section 12 as Section 13 to maintain clear organization in the Charter.

measures.questionText: Shall Article II, Section 11 of the Home Rule Charter of the Town of North Smithfield be amended to provide that members of the Board of Canvassers and Registration are appointed by the Town Council rather than elected by the Town Council, in accordance with R.I. Gen. Laws § 17-8-1 requiring a bipartisan canvassing authority appointed by the municipal legislative body?
measures.officialStatement: Currently, North Smithfield's Town Council “elects” members to the Board of Canvassers and Registration through an internal council vote. This amendment would change the process to “appointment” by the Town Council, which aligns with State law requirements. Under Rhode lsland law, the Town Council must appoint a three-member bipartisan canvassing authority with no more than two members from the same political party (R.I. Gen. Law § 17-8-1). The Council President nominates candidates from lists submitted by political party committees, and the Town Council approves the appointments. This ensures proper bipartisan representation in election oversight and brings the Charter into compliance with state requirements.

measures.questionText: Shall Article III, Section 8(c) of the Home Rule Charter of the Town of North Smithfield be amended by replacing the word "hiring" with the word "borrowing" in reference to the Town Council's authority to authorize tax anticipation notes and related municipal financing?
measures.officialStatement: This is a simple word correction to fix an error in the Charter. The current Charter incorrectly uses the word “hiring” when describing the Town Council's authority to authorize tax anticipation notes and municipal financing. Since tax anticipation notes are a form of municipal borrowing, not hiring, the word should be “borrowing”. This technical correction aligns the Charter language with the actual legal nature of these financial instruments and eliminates confusion.

provenance.quote: Shall Article III, Section 8(c) of the Home Rule Charter of the Town of North Smithfield be amended by replacing the word "hiring" with the word "borrowing" in reference to the Town Council's authority to authorize tax anticipation notes and related municipal financing?

measures.questionText: Shall Article IV, Section 9 of the Home Rule Charter of the Town of North Smithfield be amended to allow public notice of proposed ordinances and regulations to be published electronically on the Secretary of State's website in lieu of newspaper publication, in accordance with R.I. Gen. Laws § 45-6-1(c)?
measures.officialStatement: Currently, when the town wants to adopt or change ordinances and regulations, it must publish advance notice in local newspapers. This amendment would allow the town to publish these notices electronically on the Secretary of State's official website instead of in newspapers. Rhode lsland law specifically permits municipalities to use electronic notice on the Secretary of State's website in lieu of newspaper publication (R.I. Gen. Laws § 45-6-1(c)). This modernizes the notification process while maintaining public access to information about proposed local laws, and may reduce costs associated with newspaper publication requirements.

measures.officialStatement: This amendment updates the charter to conform with current state audit requirements. Rhode lsland law requires each municipality to hire independent certified public accountants to conduct detailed annual audits of the town's financial records (R.I. Gen. Laws § 45-10-4). The law also requires that the selection of auditors must receive final approval from the Rhode lsland Auditor General before the town can enter into a contract for audit services (R.I. Gen. Laws § 45-10-4). This amendment ensures North Smithfield's Charter reflects these state-mandated audit procedures and oversight requirements.

measures.questionText: Shall Article XII, Section 2 of the Home Rule Charter of the Town of North Smithfield be amended to provide that the Planning Board's powers and duties include those set forth in R.I. Gen. Laws § 45-22-7, and to update public notice requirements for Comprehensive Plan adoption or amendment in accordance with R.I. Gen. Laws § 45-22.2-8, including expanded newspaper, municipal posting, and website notice requirements?
measures.officialStatement: This amendment updates the Planning Board's powers and duties to include those specifically outlined in state law, and revises public notice requirements for adopting or amending the town's Comprehensive Plan. State law gives planning boards extensive responsibilities including preparing comprehensive plans, overseeing land development regulations, and conducting community studies. The amendment also updates notice requirements to comply with state law, which requires multiple forms of public notice including newspaper publication for three successive weeks, posting in municipal buildings, and website accessibility at least fourteen days before hearings.

measures.questionText: Shall Article XIV, Section 5 of the Home Rule Charter of the Town of North Smithfield be amended to clarify that the powers and duties of the School Committee are in addition to those set forth in R.I. Gen. Laws § 16-2-9?
measures.officialStatement: This amendment clarifies that the School Committee's powers and duties include those provided under state law. Rhode lsland law gives school committees comprehensive authority over public school interests, including educational governance, personnel decisions, and financial management. However, there is an important legal consideration: under Rhode lsland Supreme Court precedent, charter provisions affecting school committees may require express ratification by the General Assembly to be fully effective, since school committees are considered agents of the state rather than purely local bodies.

measures.questionText: Shall Article XVI, Section 8 of the Home Rule Charter of the Town of North Smithfield be amended to replace existing local ethics provisions with a requirement that all town officials and employees comply with the Rhode Island Code of Ethics, R.I. Gen. Laws § 36-14-1 et seq.?
measures.officialStatement: This amendment would replace any existing local ethics provisions in the charter with a requirement that all town officials and employees comply with the Rhode lsland Code of Ethics. The state Code of Ethics already applies to all municipal officials and employees, requiring adherence to high ethical standards, avoiding conflicts of interest, and not using public positions for private gain. This amendment would eliminate potentially conflicting local ethics rules and ensure the town operates under the uniform statewide ethics standards that apply to all Rhode lsland municipalities.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Beginning December 1, 2028, keep five council members elected townwide at regular elections in even-numbered years, but move to staggered four-year terms. In 2028, the top three candidates would receive terms ending December 1, 2032; the next two would receive terms ending December 1, 2030. Later elections would fill only expiring seats, and members would serve until successors qualify. Keep the eight-consecutive-year limit in the same elected office and the four-year break before returning. As a one-time exception, members elected in 2028 could complete their terms even if they exceed that limit. The transitional two-year terms would not count toward the limit, and those members could run for four-year terms in 2030.
